medium.title: Nifty IT Logs Best Weekly Gains Since October 2025
medium.summary:
The Nifty IT index posted its strongest weekly performance since October 2025, rebounding sharply following a broader sell-off in Asian AI and semiconductor equities. Q1 earnings results from major Indian IT firms showed limited disruption from AI adoption, which helped restore investor confidence and triggered short-covering across the sector. For equity-focused fund managers with Nifty/Sensex exposure, this IT-led rally is a notable positive given the sector's significant index weighting — IT stocks typically account for roughly 12–15% of Nifty 50. A sustained recovery in IT could provide broad index support. However, the article offers limited macro or FX read-through; INR implications remain indirect at best, as stronger IT earnings seasonally support dollar inflows via repatriation of offshore revenues.

medium.title: Oil Settles Up on Renewed US-Iran Hostilities and Threat of Red Sea Closure
medium.summary:
Oil prices surged to their highest level in over a month as US-Iran hostilities intensified, with escalating attacks across the Gulf region raising the prospect of Strait of Hormuz closure. Saudi Arabia has already begun rerouting crude exports to avoid the strait, signalling serious disruption risk to global supply chains. For India — the world's third-largest crude importer — this is a material macro concern. A sustained crude rally would widen India's trade deficit and current account deficit, exerting direct depreciation pressure on the INR/USD. Higher import costs would also feed through to domestic fuel prices, complicating the RBI's inflation management outlook and potentially delaying any future rate easing cycle. Bond markets should watch for any fiscal slippage risk if the government intervenes on fuel prices. INR traders should monitor crude closely — Brent breaking and holding above recent highs would be a key bearish trigger for the rupee.
